question: Should OpenClaw core accept model-elected continuation tools and cross-session delegate returns as an opt-in first-party agent lifecycle feature?
rationale: The PR creates new config, protocol, plugin SDK, persisted state, session lifecycle, and security-boundary behavior, so automation cannot decide whether this belongs in core or what proof bar maintainers require.

options.title: Require exact-head proof before merge
options.body: Keep the feature direction open but require maintainer product/security approval plus exact-head live receipts for continuation, delegate return, and request_compaction success before landing.

options.title: Accept as experimental opt-in
options.body: Merge with the current default-off design and proof corpus while maintainers explicitly own the remaining upgrade and boundary risk.

options.title: Split the feature
options.body: Pause this PR and ask for smaller owner-reviewed PRs that separate config/schema, continuation tools, delegate routing, and compaction behavior.

recommendation.title: Require exact-head proof before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the feature direction open but require maintainer product/security approval plus exact-head live receipts for continuation, delegate return, and request_compaction success before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history points most strongly to this owner for the central agent/runtime surfaces affected by the feature.
